script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Unseen Bond

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JANE (mid-30s, kind eyes, friendly smile) sits alone at a corner table, engrossed in a novel. The door swings open and in walks MARK (early 40s, rugged features, warm eyes). He spots Jane from across the room and approaches.

MARK
(cheerfully)
Hi, Jane. I see you're still lost in your book.

JANE
(laughs)
Hello, Mark. Yes, I am. This one's a good one.

MARK
I'll take your word for it. Fancy joining me for a cup of coffee?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - TABLE

Jane and Mark sit down at a table, facing each other.

JANE
Sure, Mark. Black, no sugar, please.

MARK
Coming right up.

They exchange small talk as the barista brings them their coffees.

MARK
So, how's work going these days?

JANE
It's been better. I got a new project that I'm really excited about.

MARK
That's great news. I remember how passionate you were about your work when we first met.

JANE
(smiling)
Yes, you do. It's been a while since we last caught up.

MARK
(nods)
Too long, indeed.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits on her couch, her laptop open in front of her. She receives a message from Mark.

JANE
(aloud)
Hi, Mark.

MARK
(via message)
I was thinking about you today and wanted to check in. How's the new project coming along?

JANE
(typing)
It's going well. I've almost finished the proposal. Thanks for asking.

MARK
(via message)
I'm so proud of you, Jane. I knew you'd make it happen.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane and Mark meet again, this time at an outdoor table. They share stories about their lives and laugh at each other's jokes.

MARK
(looking at Jane)
You know, I've always thought of you as a kindred spirit.

JANE
(surprised)
Really? I didn't know that.

MARK
Yes. We may not have seen each other for a long time, but I've always felt a strong connection to you.

JANE
(smiling)
I feel the same way, Mark. Our friendship means a lot to me.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits on her bed, staring at a picture of her and Mark from years ago. She types out a message.

JANE
(typing)
Mark, I want you to know how much I value our friendship. I don't think I would have made it through some of the toughest times in my life without you.

MARK
(via message)
Jane, that means the world to me. I feel the same way about you.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane and Mark meet yet again, this time with a purpose. They sit down at a table, their laptops open between them. They work side by side, offering suggestions and support as they edit each other's writing.

MARK
(looking up from his laptop)
You know, Jane, our bond has evolved over the years. From childhood friends to colleagues, we've grown together in so many ways.

JANE
(smiling)
Yes, it's been a beautiful journey. I'm so grateful for you, Mark.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits at her desk, surrounded by piles of papers and books. She receives a message from Mark.

MARK
(via message)
I just wanted to check in and see how your project is going. I have faith in you, Jane.

JANE
(typing)
Thank you, Mark. Your support means everything to me. I don't know what I'd do without you.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane and Mark celebrate the completion of their projects, raising their coffees in a toast to their friendship.

MARK
To us, Jane. To the unseen bond that has carried us through the years.

JANE
To us, Mark. And to many more adventures together.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
